title: Tune a Query From the Plan, Not a Folklore Index
objective: Load a dataset large enough that plans differ, capture EXPLAIN ANALYZE with actual time and buffers before and after a change, keep one index that helped, and reject one that did not.
whyThisMatters: Year-1 PostgreSQL work in the software-engineering path asks you to interpret EXPLAIN. This task requires actual times, buffer counts, and a rejected index with numbers. 'The query uses an index' is not the same as 'the query is fast.'
evidence: A note stating the loaded row count (at least 100,000 rows, or a mentor-approved equivalent)
EXPLAIN ANALYZE text for the target query before any index change, including actual time and at least one buffer statistic
EXPLAIN ANALYZE text after the kept index, with actual time and the same buffer statistic
EXPLAIN ANALYZE text for a second index (or the same query with a different index) that did not cut actual time by at least 20%, with both actual times quoted
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The dataset note states a row count of at least 100,000, or a mentor-written exception naming why a smaller set still changes the plan.
Before and after EXPLAIN ANALYZE outputs are committed as text and each quotes actual total time plus shared hits or shared reads.
The kept index is the one whose after actual time is lower than the before actual time; both times are quoted from the plans.
A second index is documented with before/after actual times showing less than 20% improvement or a regression, and it is not the recommended default.
